note: Proposed labels for the 21 generated explanations that carry no planted error, read by Claude on 2026-11-13. Not expert labels.

aid-chain-of-thought::hospital-pharmacis: Accurate. Working a vancomycin calculation on paper is a fair comparison.
aid-prompt-template::pharmacist: Accurate. A counseling script with fill-in fields is a fair comparison.
data-row::pharmacist: Accurate. One row in an allergy table maps to one patient's allergy entry.
sys-enum::hospital-pharmacist: An allergy field limited to four values (NKDA, penicillin, sulfa, latex) is not realistic. Allergy fields draw on large coded allergen lists.
sec-secret::pharmacist: A DEA number is not a secret. It is printed on prescriptions and shared with pharmacies routinely, so the comparison is false.
sec-secret::hospital-pharmacist: Automated dispensing cabinet override is a function tied to a user's own credentials, not a shared 'Pyxis override code' or combination.
sec-sso::hospital-pharmacist: Accurate. Badge-tap single sign-on into clinical systems is common.
sec-vulnerability::hospital-pharmacist: The drug-interaction comparison for urgency is loose but not false.
web-domain::hospital-pharmacist: Accurate. A domain change is a reasonable hint that a system moved.
web-status-code::pharmacist: Paid claims carry no reject code. Paid or rejected is a separate response status, and reject codes explain rejections (75 means prior authorization required).
cloud-log::nurse: Compares logs to nursing charting that is careful not to include anything sensitive, but charting is full of protected health information by necessity.
cloud-log::hospital-pharmacist: Same comparison: chart entries are described as made without exposing anything sensitive, which is not how clinical documentation works.
cloud-observability::nurse: Accurate. Continuous monitoring is a fair comparison.
cloud-observability::hospital-pharmacist: Accurate. Vitals and trends for a septic patient are a fair comparison.
